ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening under PCMLTFA/FINTRAC guidance, including verification of foreign politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates; enhanced due diligence for medium-risk social-casino gaming using Apple IAP and Google Play Billing; screening against Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and relevant domestic designated persons lists; results to be documented and refreshed upon material change or at least every 90 days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec - Registre des entreprises (official online portal: registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, the enterprise name must be in French; words from another language are permitted only as registered trademarks or distinctive approved elements; the legal designation must be expressed in French as 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.'; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin script with the French version given equal or greater prominence in Quebec business communications.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the Registraire des entreprises du Québec issues a written refusal stating grounds; the applicant may file a written reconsideration request within 30 days of notification, attaching corrected French-compliant names, trademark certificates where applicable, and supporting legal submissions. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Court of Québec under the applicable provisions of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises and the Code of Civil Procedure. A valid name reservation may be extended by requesting an extension before expiry; extension decisions are discretionary and, if granted, are typically granted for an additional period of up to 90 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or serviced office is permissible for an unlicensed Quebec limited partnership during the pre-licensing phase, provided a registered agent in Quebec accepts service of process and maintains statutory records; financial institutions and payment processors may nevertheless reject a virtual-only office for merchant underwriting, and any future gaming or liquor/gaming authorization from the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux may require a physical establishment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk is approximately 10% in the first 12 months for a non-licensed, virtual social-casino publisher; the risk rises to roughly 20-25% if enhanced merchant due diligence by payment service providers or FINTRAC supervisory activity triggers a records or physical-site compliance verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236–2248 (limited partnership / société en commandite) and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 3–16 (registration, name reservation, compulsory disclosure)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Québec limited partnership. Each limited partner must contribute only the amount agreed in the partnership agreement; contribution may be cash, property, or services. The limited partner's liability is limited to the unpaid balance of the promised contribution. No mandatory escrow deposit is imposed by the Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF THE LIMITED PARTNERSHIP. RESOLVED: (1) The initial subscriptions and capital contributions of the limited partners, as recorded in the Limited Partnership Agreement, are approved and accepted. (2) The registered office is established at [full address], Province of Québec, and the Québec Enterprise Registrar is directed to record that address. (3) [Name], as general partner, is designated to exercise management authority, and [Name] is appointed as administrator/officer responsible for day-to-day operations. (4) The general partner and any officer are authorized to execute and file the Declaration of Registration, to open bank accounts, and to engage professional advisors. (5) All acts taken in furtherance hereof are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online platform (Espace clients / Enterprise Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary name search in the enterprise register. If the proposed name is not likely to be confused with other registered names and complies with the rules of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, submit an online Name Reservation Request with the proposed legal name and complete the declaration.
required_dossiers: Basic identification of each partner (name, address, date of birth for individuals or legal entity identifiers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit an amended name request or appeal the decision within the review procedure set out in section 34 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders and the general partner, advised by legal counsel; notarization is required only for contributions of real property or certain hypothecs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a written limited partnership agreement identifying each general and limited partner, the nature of the business, capital contributions, profit and loss allocation, management rights, and dissolution terms. Ensure each partner executes the agreement and each limited partner acknowledges the intent to contribute the agreed amount.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement signed by all partners
Consent of the general partner to act as such
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner disputes a term, amend the agreement by supplementary written instrument or execute a restated limited partnership agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Enterprise Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership (Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite). Include the partnership name, the registered office address in Québec, the name and address of the general partner, and a statement of aggregate limited partner contributions. Pay the applicable registration fee electronically and obtain the certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Completed and signed Declaration of Registration
Consent of the general partner to the registration
Copy of the limited partnership agreement if requested by the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of irregularity, correct the specific information online and resubmit within the stated cure period (generally 10 business days) or the registration will be cancelled.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax Filings and Business Number Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (Quebec Revenue Agency) and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the certificate of registration, register the limited partnership with the CRA for a federal business number and with Revenu Québec for the Québec enterprise number, the QST account if the partnership makes taxable supplies in Québec, and any employer payroll accounts. File the initial declaration with Revenu Québec and update the enterprise register with all statutory disclosures.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration from the Registraire des entreprises
Identification of all partners and the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a filing is queried or rejected, resubmit the corrected information through the respective online portals; missing information may be cured within 30 days without penalty.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial manufacturing licence is required for online software publishing. If the partnership were to operate a real-money gaming venue, the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux (RACJ) would have jurisdiction, but social-casino software distribution through app stores does not constitute regulated gambling under the Criminal Code (Canada).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None mandated; optional compliance certifications (e.g., ISO/IEC 27001) and app-store provider terms apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category X (said activity is digital publishing; no significant environmental footprint; no EIA required).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to cloud-based operations; office premises must comply with municipal waste handling, electrical/electronic equipment recycling (Recyclage Québec), and general ventilation and energy efficiency norms.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety compliance certificate under the Québec Fire Safety Code for any occupied commercial premises; municipal certificate of occupancy attesting structural load and safe egress; and an occupational health and safety program under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c. S-2.1) applicable to employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) through Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/businesses/business-number-registration.html); for Quebec provincial tax and enterprise registry: Revenu Québec (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/) and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) or an extra-provincial limited partnership carrying on business in Quebec: (1) file the declaration/registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) to obtain the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ); (2) register for the federal CRA Business Number (BN) using Business Registration Online; (3) register for GST/HST by filing Form RC1 with the CRA unless the partnership qualifies as a small supplier; (4) register separately with Revenu Québec for QST using the NEQ, completing the registration questionnaire and, where applicable, electing a representative for service of documents; and (5) maintain all partnership constituent documents, general partner identities and ownership records in English or French for verification by CRA or Revenu Québec. The LP itself is not a legal person under Quebec civil law, but for GST/HST and QST purposes it is a separate registrant; therefore the registration must be in the partnership's own name and administered by the general partner.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no U.S.-style 'check-the-box' election; tax classification is determined by legal form. A Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent for federal and Quebec income tax: income or loss is allocated to partners, each of whom computes tax in his/her/its own jurisdiction. For GST/HST and QST, however, the partnership is a 'person' liable for registration, collection and remittance. There is no elective transparent/opaque classification for Canadian income tax purposes. Hybrid mismatch elections are not available; Canada applies anti-hybrid rules which may deny deductions where partnership transparency interacts inconsistently with a foreign tax system. Relief-elected periods or fiscal-period elections may be available only in the narrow circumstances prescribed under the Income Tax Act, principally for partnership fiscal years; non-resident partners should separately assess the section 253 deemed-carrying-on-business rule and any applicable treaty permanent establishment protection.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST) (provincial VAT-type consumption tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST and QST small-supplier threshold: CAD 30,000 in total worldwide taxable supplies over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters, with QST effectively requiring CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies attributable to Quebec; registration becomes mandatory once the threshold is exceeded, and optional below it.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: There is no generalized real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control regime, or mandatory digital stamping for GST/HST or QST in Canada/Quebec. The CRA and Revenu Québec accept electronic invoicing, but require prescribed invoice particulars for GST/HST and QST, including seller/registrant identification, transaction description, tax rates and amounts. Periodic GST/HST and QST returns are electronically filed through CRA and Revenu Québec portals, and certain high-volume registrants may have enhanced electronic reporting obligations. Apple/Google payment rails do not perform tax clearance or stamping; the regulated supplier remains responsible for tax compliance on each simulated casual-game transaction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available on supplies of goods exported directly by the supplier and on qualifying exported services/intangible personal property supplied to a non-resident recipient who is not registered under GST/HST, where the supply is not made in Canada under the place-of-supply rules. For social-casino and virtual-slots digital gaming services, zero-rating will generally require documented evidence of the recipient's residence outside Canada, including payment-rail address, billing country, IP/geolocation data, and dedicated backend records. Supplies made to Canadian-resident consumers through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing are taxable in Canada at the applicable GST/HST plus QST rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian customs export declaration (B13A/CERS electronic export declaration
Bill of lading or equivalent transport/waybill evidence showing export from Canada
Inward remittance certificate or foreign exchange/conversion record establishing receipt of funds from the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may deny a zero-rated export claim or refund where the supporting export/remittance documentation is incomplete or internally inconsistent. Under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec QST Act, making a false or misleading statement, failing to provide records, or participating in a fraudulent zero-rating scheme can result in interest, penalties, gross-negligence penalties of up to 50% of the tax claimed or avoided, reassessment beyond the normal four-year limitation period in cases of misrepresentation or wilful default, and prosecution. Clawbacks typically include the full zero-rated amount originally claimed, disallowed input tax credits, interest computed from the balance-due date, and any assessed penalty.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange oversight is conducted under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) by FINTRAC and by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for regulated financial institutions. There is no dedicated foreign exchange control administration in Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains unrestricted current- and capital-account convertibility under the Bank of Canada Act and the Currency Act. There are no exchange controls restricting profit remittance, capital inflows, or liquidation proceeds. The Canadian dollar trades freely; however, FINTRAC and Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) impose mandatory reporting on cash, currency, and monetary instruments equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000, and cross-border wire transfers are subject to record-keeping and sanctions-screening protocols.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Exporters may retain foreign currency proceeds indefinitely or convert them at commercial discretion. FINTRAC reporting thresholds apply to large cash transactions and international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more; CBSA requires physical cross-border reporting of currency or monetary instruments at CAD 10,000 or above.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for primary treasury banking; MEDIUM as supplementary payment facilitation. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) licensed in the EEA or UK are not recognized as deposit-taking institutions in Canada. They can operate only if registered as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) with FINTRAC and may not open CAD clearing accounts unless through a Canadian bank partner. For the LP's treasury, direct use of an offshore EMI is legally constrained; Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlement requires clearance into a Canadian-chartered bank account or a FINTRAC-registered payment processor.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and the general partner are not statutorily required to appear physically for all account openings; Canadian banks may permit remote onboarding using audio-video identity verification under FINTRAC-accredited methods. In practice, tier-1 banks mandate an in-person or notarized meeting (at a Canadian branch or before a recognized notary) for a Limited Partnership with non-resident beneficial owners in the medium-risk social casino vertical, to validate the partnership agreement, signing authority, source of funds, and beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Product misclassification as real-money gambling or wagering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a Quebec-licensed counsel legal opinion classifying the simulated social casino as non-gambling under the Criminal Code (Canada) and the Act respecting lotteries, publicity, and amusement machines (L.R.Q., c. L-6); include product terms of service, virtual currency mechanics, no-cash-out functionality, and App Store/Google Play category confirmation of 'non-gambling social casino.'

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Limited Partnership ownership opacity and non-resident partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a complete register of general and limited partners; notarized certified copies of the Quebec limited partnership registration (Registraire des entreprises), the executed partnership agreement, certificate of existence, and beneficial ownership declarations; execute PEP and sanctions screening reports confirming no adverse media, PEP, or OFAC/EU/UN sanctions hits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity digital in-app purchase settlement and aggregated payouts from Apple/Google
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Implement a treasury reconciliation perimeter linking Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console financial reports to bank settlement statements; provide contractual agreements with Apple Inc. and Google LLC, audited revenue recognition reports, and an explanatory memo on the aggregated settlement cadence; keep transactional source data available for triggered audit.

Compile a source-of-funds questionnaire for each contributing partner; include bank reference letters from originating institutions; provide tax-residency certificates and confirm compliance with the Income Tax Act and Quebec Taxation Act; run continuous sanctions screening and retain evidence of no restricted-party relationships.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from non-resident partners should be remitted by SWIFT MT103 to the LP's Canadian-dollar account at a Canadian chartered bank, using purpose code 'Capital contribution / Direct investment into Canadian limited partnership' (Statistics Canada/OECD BMD4 code '4' or bank-defined direct-investment indicator). Correspondent banks must be verified for sanctions compliance; any physical currency or monetary instrument equal to or above CAD 10,000 transported across the border must be reported to CBSA, and FINTRAC reporting applies to large international electronic funds transfers of CAD 10,000 or more. Supporting documents must include the executed partnership agreement, calling capital notices, bank reference from the remitting bank, and source-of-wealth statements for each limited partner.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational outflows, including licensing fees, developer royalty payments, and app-store commission settlements, should be cleared via SWIFT MT103 for international transfers. For large physical procurement (e.g., packaging or hardware), a SWIFT MT700 Commercial Letter of Credit may be used. Domestic CAD clearing within Canada is executed through Payments Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or, where available, the Real-Time Rail (RTR) for immediate retail payments. Apple IAP and Google Play Billing gross settlements are inbound disbursements settled by Apple and Google to the LP's operating account; outbound partnerships are structured through direct bank wires.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) (for currencies of limited convertibility; CAD is fully deliverable, so NDFs may be used administratively for exotic B2B counterparties)
Exchange-Traded Currency Futures (via Canadian regulated markets)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the last day of the month following the month containing the registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 30–CAD 100 per the applicable REQ tariff; continued non-filing after a formal reminder notice may result in cancellation of registration, which triggers deemed dissolution of the limited partnership.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return (T5013) and related T5013 slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); Revenu Québec where the partnership has Québec establishment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year; for a non-calendar fiscal period, within three months after the fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA late-filing penalty: CAD 25 per partner per day, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500; continued failure may also trigger criminal prosecution or summary conviction fines.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit is imposed on a private Quebec limited partnership under the Civil Code of Quebec or the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. A mandatory independent audit arises only where: (i) the limited partnership is a reporting issuer under securities legislation; (ii) the partnership agreement requires an auditor; or (iii) the entity becomes subject to the audit requirement of a corporate general partner registered under the Quebec Business Corporations Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; ASPE (Canadian GAAP) for private entities; partnership accounts must be prepared on a GAAP basis and reconciled to the tax-basis partnership calculation set out in applicable Canada and Québec tax laws.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The REQ annual declaration requires each enterprise to confirm current individuals who hold, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of the partnership rights. Any transfer of a partnership interest resulting in a new 25% beneficial owner must be filed with REQ as an amendment within 15 days of the change; the annual declaration then serves as the annual confirmation that the disclosed beneficial ownership remains accurate or has been updated.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for a non-reporting private LP; voluntary certified audit typically USD 4,500 - 18,000 depending on transaction volume and consolidated group structure

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); for this limited partnership, the rate is pass-through to partners and no entity-level income tax applies to the LP itself
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal small business deduction (for CCPC corporate partners) on first C$500,000 of qualifying active business income lowers combined rate to about 12.2%; refundable SR&ED federal investment tax credit up to 35% and Quebec R&D/digital-media tax credits can reduce effective cost; non-capital loss carryforward of 20 years (3-year carryback)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal T5013 'Partnership Information Return' and T5013 slips filed through CRA's Internet File Transfer Service / Form T5 or T5013 filing system; a corporate partner's own income is filed as T2 via CRA e-File
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (partnership fiscal-period information return; corporate partners must also pay quarterly tax instalments if required)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: March 31 of the following calendar year for a December 31 fiscal period end; for a non-calendar fiscal period, within five months after the fiscal period end; T2 corporate returns are due six months after the corporation's taxation year-end

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Identification block (legal name, BN/RC account, type of partnership)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the full LP legal name, Quebec enterprise number, CRA business number, and the fiscal period start/end dates; confirm whether the LP has a permanent establishment in Quebec and whether any non-resident partner holds an interest in an 'inactive partnership'.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If non-resident partners exist, report their full name, address, and country of residence; the LP must obtain all partners' social insurance or business numbers where available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 Box 130-180 (Income and expenses by source)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the partnership's gross revenue and deductible expenses (software publishing and in-app sales net of platform commissions), cost of goods sold, amortization, royalties, and any Part IV/refundable tax adjustments if the partnership has a corporate partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners' shares are calculated using the same source rules as Canadian taxpayers; a foreign partner carrying on business in Canada through the LP must compute Part I tax on the share of Canadian business income, with a treaty-protected exemption only if no permanent establishment is present in Canada/Quebec.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 Schedule 2 - Allocation of partnership income (loss) and partner identification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocate net income/loss to general and limited partners according to the LP agreement; losses must not exceed a limited partner's 'at-risk amount' (contributed capital and loans attributable to the partnership).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border allocations must satisfy the OECD AOA/certainty; a non-resident limited partner claiming loss allocations must be able to substantiate an interest in the LP and actual business use; for non-arm's-length transactions, attach T106 schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 Box 172-199 (Part II tax, CPEO and other partner-specific entries)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify whether the LP is a 'Canadian partnership' under ITA s. 102, whether it has a CPA or CPE; if corporate partners are CCPCs, describe each partner's share of 'active business' or 'property income' for the SBD and refundable Part IV tax computation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners' allocations from Canadian-source income are subject to Part I (business income) or Part XIII (rents/royalties/interest) depending on the character; treaty-resident partners should attach Form NR301 or equivalent to claim reduced withholding.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file T5013/Summary: CRA penalty of C$100 plus C$25 per late day up to C$2,500, plus further penalties for each T5013 slip not filed; corporate T2 late filing: 5% of balance due plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; Quebec TP-600 late penalty similarly scaled under the Tax Administration Act, generally C$100 to C$1,500 or more; criminal sanctions for false returns can reach 200% of tax evaded plus imprisonment.
